name: Card networks

naics.title: Financial Transactions Processing, Reserve, and Clearinghouse Activities

one_line: Runs the rails that move a card payment from a shopper's bank to a store's bank, and takes a small cut of each one.
sells: Payment authorization, clearing and settlement, charged per transaction and per dollar
customers: Card-issuing banks and the merchant acquirers that sign up stores
suppliers: Data centers, fraud and security technology

revenue.metric: combined net revenue of the two largest networks
revenue.note: Excludes American Express, UnionPay, Discover and JCB.

structure.why: Visa and Mastercard are the two global open networks most banks issue cards on; Visa alone carried 40.76% of global card purchase transactions in 2025 (Nilson). Each new card and store makes the network more valuable to the other side.
structure.hhi_note: Not computed: only Visa's share of global transactions is public.

econ: Two-sided network effects: shoppers want the card every store takes, stores take the card every shopper carries, so the two leaders are very hard to dislodge.

companies.name: Visa
companies.share_basis: share of global card purchase transactions, 2025 (Nilson Report)

companies.name: UnionPay
companies.note: China's card network; one of the six global networks the Nilson Report tracks.

companies.name: American Express
companies.note: Closed loop: issues its own cards and signs up its own merchants.
